for_you_if: you enjoy mastering distinct character playstyles
you want deep tactical card combat
not_for_you_if: you dislike heavy randomness in card draws
you struggle with punishing elite encounters

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game relies heavily on randomness and luck with card draws and run outcomes, which can lead to frustrating or doomed runs.

citations.review_text: A little more random than I might like - some runs feel doomed fairly quickly, but overall lots of tactical fun!

Felt like complete luck. No discernable progression as you start over from nothing with every attempt. Somehow the monsters coincidentally are strong in exactly the way that exploits your deck. Just awful.

I want to like this game but good lord the RNG is so annoying. Every strategy guide says thin your deck (a very basic strategy for deck builders) but the only way I can find to do that is at shops? And I only hit 3 shops a run? And the cost to delete a card goes up every time? 
Everything about this game feels designed to frustrate you and screw you over.

A good, hard and frustrating game all at the same time, Slay the Spire will make you feel the pain of every fall and the glory of every victory. Climb 50 levels just to get obliterated by the OP boss in Act 3 everytime with every character, swear you'll never play again, then return to the game tomorrow without exceptions. If RNG smiles at you, you might do better next time, but completely slaying the whole spire is going to be an actual mountain to conquer.

If what I've said above made you think it's not fun, you'd be wrong. Without the tough fights, unlucky deaths, seemingly cursed luck, Slay the Spire would lose part of its appeal. Every card you pick and decision you make will shape the run without you even knowing how much yet, only to find out later. Although not perfect, Slay the Spire manages to convey onto the player the exact feelings of dread the characters feel everytime we embark on a journey.

Relies too heavily on luck to strengthen your builds and secure your run. This is one of those "As you lose your character gets stronger" games which is a mechanic I strongly dislike if it's done as distasteful as this game does it (my opinion).

Skill and strategy are irrelevant, has no meaning in this game. Sheer luck.

Because HP goes too fast for the player but more often than not it goes too slow for the enemies. Too many times do you find yourself as a player with 80hp going against 2 or 3 enemies with 12hp each and they're dishing out more damage than your character can. They're shattering your shields with ease and out damaging you. And for some reason they will keep showing up with high buff values despite the fact the run just started less than 5 minutes ago.

Healing is a joke for 2 reasons:
1. You need to heal at camp fires but they heal a laughably small fixed value of your health, and they have rng appearance with only 1 guaranteed spot of spawning right before the final boss of the area.
         - Many times you will see camp fires for healing on your map surrounded by enemies too risky to 
            engage with.
         - To make them heal more you can find (RNG) items that increase a little % of the heal granted.

2. The merchant's appearance is RNG
        - You need Gold to buy from him
        - Your gold can be robbed by the thief enemies if you do not kill them fast enough
        - He may not be travelling with a heal when you see him (Notice how I implied 1 healing item not 
           multiple.)

You could play as smart as you want with what you find but the damage enemies do to the player vs how much damage the player can return will often times be ridiculously unbalanced because of how RNG this game is. I don't find it fun when my wins rely more on luck than strategy.

I don't find it fun when the whole point of this game is to build and survive but you get punished for trying to prepare for a fight and you get puni…

Not really for me. The gameplay itself is okay if you like deckbuilders that have a lot of randomness built into them by design. I realize that that is on purpose and that it forces the player to adapt to each situation but I do find some runs to be incredibly boring because you're unlucky with your draws. There's little to no story, no lore and the graphics and animations are not doing a good job of keeping me engaged. The music is serviceable but nothimg special.

This is a card based game where you fight battles over and over and it pretends to be a rogue/rogue - light.


There are 4 characters, the iron clad, which is tanky, the silent, which is like a rouge. The other two characters I have not played. I find this game so unenjoyable that I don't feel I can keep grinding to unlock anything else.


I am not unschooled in card based games. I've played magic the gathering, yugioh, and pokemon, all of which I have enjoyed.


At the start of the spire, you decide on a special effect/buff. You start with 10 cards in your deck and 3 mana points. Cards have mana cost displayed at the top of cards. You start the game with 5 cards in your hand. After playing your turn, you discard your entire hand and draw a new hand. When your deck is exhausted, your discard pile is shuffled and recycled.


Combat: At the start of your turn you will see icons above enemy heads. This tells you if they intend to attack, defend, play buffs or de-buffs. Based on the cards in your hand, decide whether to attack and take damage and try to burn the enemy down, or defend and withstand attacks. Your cards can poison or reduce the strength or attack of enemies.


Why this game is absolutely trash: You don't get to build a starting deck. Many of the cards have lots of synergy, so getting to decide on some other cards at the start besides base attack or base block would be more enjoyable. After enemies are defeated, you get gold, sometimes potions with special effects, and you can add 1 card to your deck. As you progress, you can encounter a trader to by cards and potions. If you encounter a campfire, you can decide on healing or upgrading a card. Lastly, cards you have upgraded as you play don't stay upgraded when you die. Your heroes get no keepable buffs either.


This creates a game that is entirely dependent on RNG, without ANY character growth, and minimal chances to strategize. Not sure if any of that changes as your game levels up death after death. It'…

cohorts.summary: Mid-tier players praise varied playstyles and mods while clashing over steep learning curves and punishing random drops.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as heavily reliant on RNG for card and relic drops, which can lead to frustrating runs when necessary items are not received.

citations.review_text: Full disclosure, I am not a seasoned rogue lite fan. But, Slay The Spire does have great variety of items and power ups. And a good art style and music soundtrack. However, I think the RNG can be a bit too janky and punishing. Perhaps I can't appreciate the joy of doing a glorious 2 hour run for the final ending with a the one and only Boss having a second form.

Been hooked for 48 hours of gameplay without mods so far. The game's RNG is frustrating, but you keep playing in hopes of a run where everything lines up and you just stomp all the bosses. It really didn't click for me until I unlocked all the characters and found one I really liked.

Fun idea and very addicting gameplay. But 100% RNG. Read dozens of different guides and deck lists. Tried to follow them. Never got the necessary cards dropped to properly build those decks in several runs. This game is unfortunately more luck than skill.

I don’t understand the hype of the overwhelmingly positive reviews. I went in expecting a gem of a roguelike. What I got was a very aggressive RNG card game that feels time is wasted the more and more I play through runs. 

Solid concept of the gameplay but you need to be extremely lucky in runs when building your deck, otherwise the entire run ends up being a waste of time just to restart from the beginning. Not only this, but the game just gets frustrating when you fight multiple enemies at a time or when a boss pulls out a 30+ damage attack out of nowhere you can’t block the entirety of. I personally like rogue games that have me work towards an achievable goal that feels possible with each run. I don’t enjoy when my runs feel like a waste of time and feel like I’m accomplishing nothing. 

I love roguelikes and roguelites, but I guess this game just wasn’t for me. Maybe you’ll enjoy it if you enjoy card games. If I could recommend a different rogue card game, I’d say Inscryption.

StS does a better job hiding the fact that it's a slot machine than most modern roguelikes, but make no mistake -- it's still a slot machine.  Pray you get the best relics and some kind of damage and defense scaling, something that you have literally zero control over.  If the game deigns to give you what you need, you win; if you don't, you lose.

I've been slaying my spire all week long. But for real, this is a great roguelike deckbuilder, lots of interesting builds and cards. The only problem I see is the fact that it's not really fair, is it? The RNG is not that forgiving, so I'd advise you to install some mods from the workshop to make it more fun and less frustrating. All in all, it's a good title. Check out Dice With Death and Rainbow Legends for a similar gameplay loop. Cheers :)

Good, not great. Decent game design with some balancing issues. Progress is dependent upon finding relics and RNG. Elite and boss fights scale disproportionally to player, with constant minion spawns, multiple cc attacks and debuffs, and basic attacks that hit for 25-40% of your HP with no counter play options. Mystery rooms are increasingly frustrating with more RNG that either leaves you with less HP or something else that is less than desired. I really like this concept at first, thinking StS would be a game I could easily spend 100 or more hours playing, but it's more annoying than fun.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features multiple playable characters with distinct progression, unique decks, and varied playstyles.

citations.review_text:
There are two things I look for in roguelikes, and Slay the Spire nails both:

1. Every run should feel unique. There have to be elements of both choice and luck that can combine in novel ways to reveal cool synergies (or amplify into a luckless trainwreck) so that you can't simply go for an autopilot strategy and do things the same every single time. Slay the Spire handles this well, both with different species you unlock that have different decks and require different playstyles, and with luck of the draw on getting different cards, potions, and relics (or getting to a shop at a time when you have the funds). Being able to choose different routes through each map also gives you some sense of agency and hope when you otherwise might feel doomed by the onslaught.

2. The difficulty should be able to be tweaked, not just slightly, but dramatically. The more punishing you want to make your game, the more range I want in choosing how hard it will be. It's not a matter of cheating or avoiding "getting good"--it's about accessibility as well as how I choose to spend the limited hours of my life. For me? I had about 20 hours of fun with Slay the Spire. By that time, I had more than gotten my money's worth and was happy to leave it there. But then I did a few juiced up runs with Custom scenarios that started me off with better cards and other perks--and I enjoyed the game for another 10 hours. I also got to enjoy "beating" some rounds by making it through all the maps. It's a testament to how challenging Slay the Spire can actually be that you can "cheat" to give yourself a ton of advantages... and still be soundly defeated if you get complacent!

But having the plethora of customization options allowed me to play Slay the Spire in a way that satisfied me and gave me closure when I felt like being done. Did I unlock everything? Not even close. But you don't need to be a die-hard completionist to enjoy this game, and that is priceless.

This is a very solid deck-building roguelike.  The different characters are interesting and fun, with a clear progression from the straightforward bruiser to the more complex.  I think it could use a bit more visual development to make it that much more engaging, perhaps.  That's not so essential in a game like this, but when I compare to, say, Slots and Daggers, which pours a lot of attention into the visual and audio development of its single gameplay screen, I see what is possible and what difference it can make.

I'm not much of completionist.  I slew the spire with 2 of the four characters (The Silent and The Defect), played a few more runs with The Defect (my favorite) after that, and did several runs with the Watcher before deciding that, while interesting, it was too frustratingly swingy for my tastes.

So, I might have wished for a few more characters or more content, but overall a solid enough game to get my recommendation.

Been hooked for 48 hours of gameplay without mods so far. The game's RNG is frustrating, but you keep playing in hopes of a run where everything lines up and you just stomp all the bosses. It really didn't click for me until I unlocked all the characters and found one I really liked.
Satisfying, unique heroes. I wish there was more variation in enemies. Daily climbs are more fun than I would've guessed.
The game has infinite replayability. Even if you complete ascension 20 on all 4 characters the game has an amazing modding community that adds even more content to try.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game experiences technical issues such as kernel security check failure crashes upon launch that require repairing game files.

citations.review_text:
Over the last 24h, I've had to repair game files twice. Or this game crashes my computer upon launch with a kernal security check failure.
Only this game. Goes away after repairing. Something's seriously wrong with your code.
850+ hours played btw

This game offers an astonishing amount of replayability and remains the gold standard for deck-building roguelikes. With countless card, relic, and character combinations to experiment with, no two runs feel quite the same. Much of the fun comes from discovering powerful synergies and assembling absurdly strong decks that can completely break the game's challenges.
The atmosphere is another strength. Despite the dangers lurking around every corner, the game maintains a consistent charm with a lighthearted and often humorous tone that makes repeated runs enjoyable rather than exhausting.
The game provides a satisfying challenge even at its default difficulty. Success requires careful deck construction, resource management, and long-term planning. Once you've mastered the basics, a wide range of additional difficulty levels offer an endless series of new obstacles and keeps the experience engaging for hundreds of hours.
My main criticism is the progression system. Unlocking all cards and relics requires some grinding early on. Similarly, new ascension levels must be unlocked one by one and separately for each character. 
Overall, this is the best deck-building game I've played and one of the defining titles of the entire genre. Its blend of strategic depth, replayability, and elegant design has influenced countless games that followed, and for good reason.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features multiple distinct playable characters with unique decks, offering different playstyles for each run.

citations.review_text:
[h1]Maybe polish your unfinished game before making a sequel[/h1]
Slay the spire has a lot of great things going for it, it has a nice "easy to understand, hard to master" feeling, there's an ok amount of enemy variety, every enemy has unique skills, there's a lot of variability with your deck-building, some random events, many items, a few playable characters, good bosses, good music, and probably other things that I'm forgetting.

My main gripe is that it is way too short, only 10 bosses (4 per run, if you can reach the last) with like 15 enemies in between, and the game is made for you to keep retrying the same adventure with little to no reward, only new skills and other unlockables, there's no ending, no final objective, just you retrying over and over thinking that maybe next time you'll do some real damage to the heart, but even if you win it is all reset with no satisfactory ending (The lore, with minimal spoilers is that Neow keeps you coming back until the heart dies, and you always come back even if you manage to cut into it).

For the high price I can't in good faith recommend this, even during steam sales I find the price too steep for what this is, and after years of waiting for a passable update, the devs just made a slay the spire 2 instead of improving the first...
